I CONFIRM codex's rescale-before-centring defect but refute its severity: I swept the payload/offset ratio on codex's own exactly-representable 512x32 Hadamard fixture and the false spike exists ONLY within ~4 ULPs of the offset (spike_energy 0.515625 at ratio 1.164e-16 and 0.225 at 4.657e-16, but already exactly 0.0 at 1.863e-15 and the KS bit-exact at 0.526593536 from 7.629e-12 upward). comparable_reason: The KS statistic against a fixed MP law is a finite-size quantity, so it shrinks with width even at a MATCHED aspect ratio. Eight iid Gaussian seeds per width, all at gamma ~ 0.25 by construction (N = 4D+8): mean raw KS 0.059018147541 / 0.033974019008 / 0.018614850041 / 0.009794592732 and mean g25 KS 0.048973740265 / 0.034006409207 / 0.017632154784 / 0.009906772197 for D = 32/64/128/256. Spearman rho = -1.0 with width for BOTH families, a 4.94x fall in the pure-noise null over an 8x width change. fixed_gamma=0.25 equalises the MP reference but not the null distribution, so a wide model scores 'closer to MP' for no structural reason. Cross-model use needs a per-width null calibration (a permutation or iid baseline at the same (N,D)), which the *_g25 keys do not provide.

github_repo: AlejandroSantorum/scikit-rmt (CDF cross-check only; Marchenko-Pastur 1967 / BBP 2005 released no code)
github_reason: Executed the installed scikit-rmt 1.3.0 MarchenkoPasturDistribution.cdf head-to-head against BLME's _mp_cdf and against my own scipy.quad reference at gamma = 0.04/0.25/0.5/0.9 x 101 interior points. scikit-rmt is the more accurate quadrature in the bulk (max error 1.4e-14 vs BLME's 1.4e-7) but is WRONG on the gamma>1 atom: at gamma=4, x=0 it returns 0.0 where the correct value is 1 - 1/gamma = 0.75, which BLME returns exactly. So the reference is a partial cross-check, not an oracle. No code was released with either source paper; the task's aggregate (permutation null, sigma^2 quantile match, fixed-gamma subsample) is BLME-original and has no reference implementation.
paper_reason: Marchenko & Pastur 1967 and Baik et al. 2005 publish laws, not experimental scalars for transformer activations, and Staats et al. 2024 (arXiv:2410.17770) reports WEIGHT singular spectra, not this activation aggregate. The only reproducible published quantities are the closed forms themselves -- support edges (1 +- sqrt(gamma))^2 and the atom mass 1 - 1/gamma -- both of which BLME reproduces with absolute error 0.0.
confounds_reason: Direct measurement, not correlation over a heterogeneous zoo: on PURE iid Gaussian noise with the aspect ratio held fixed at gamma = 0.25, the reported deviation-from-MP falls monotonically with d_model (rho = -1.0, 4.94x over D = 32 -> 256, 8 seeds each). Any cross-model ordering of this feature therefore encodes width before it encodes structure. gamma itself is reported and is D/(N-1), i.e. an explicit architecture-over-corpus ratio.
defects: CODE / RESCALE BEFORE CENTRING, THREE PLACES (rmt_bulk.py:321-323 in _mp_layer_metrics, :435-437 and :461-464 in _mp_metrics_core). Every one divides by the ACTUAL maximum -- not a power of two, so each division rounds -- and does so before the mean is subtracted, which measures the rounding against the OFFSET instead of against the payload. FIXTURE INTEGRITY VERIFIED: on X = 1e6 + spacing(1e6)*hadamard(512)[:,1:33] the round trip (X-1e6)/spacing(1e6) reproduces H exactly and np.corrcoef(X, rowvar=False) equals I_32 with max error 0.0, because corrcoef centres first; BLME instead reports outlier_frac 0.031250, spike_energy 0.515625 and ks 0.968750 against the true 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.526593536. CROSSOVER MEASURED: the artefact is gone by payload/offset = 1.863e-15 (16 ULPs) and the answer is bit-exact from 7.629e-12 upward, so it is not reachable on real activations. Same defect class the repo already fixed in matrix_entropy and schatten; the repo's own centre_and_rescale helper fixes it here too.

CODE / CDF QUADRATURE DEGRADES AS gamma -> 1 (rmt_bulk.py:82-125). The 4096-node theta grid is accurate to 1.4e-7 for gamma <= 0.9 but loses order at the lower edge as the support collapses: at gamma = 0.999 the CDF at x = 4.25e-6 is 8.393725e-4 against the true 8.514707e-4 (-1.42%), and at gamma = 7168/7169 it is 1.024347e-3 against 1.205122e-3 (-15.0%), with 1.03e-4 absolute error even at mid-support x = 2.0. task_metadata.py:61 advertises 'parity <=2.3e-5' without a gamma qualifier and that is exceeded above gamma ~ 0.999. NOT REACHABLE AT THE SHIPPED PROTOCOL: num_samples=200 supplies ~23272 tokens capped to 20000, so gpt2 runs at gamma = 768/19999 = 0.0384 and the widest zoo model (d=7168) at 0.358, where the error is <= 1.4e-7.

NORMALIZED CODE / g25 DRAW CAN TERMINATE AT THE WRONG ASPECT RATIO (rmt_bulk.py:381-390). The corrective loop runs at most 4 times and simply falls through if the realised non-constant width oscillates between two values, emitting *_g25 keys computed at whatever gamma the last draw happened to have. No achieved-gamma is emitted for the g25 family (the 3 gamma fields all describe the FULL cloud), so a consumer cannot detect it. Requires dimensions with sparse support, so low prevalence on dense activations, but the whole purpose of this family is that gamma is identical across models.
COMPARABILITY (not an implementation defect): the iid null of both KS families scales as ~D^-1/2; rho = -1.0 with width at matched gamma.

CONFIG (not an implementation defect): defaults.yaml:148 edge_tol=0.05 shifts the gamma=0.25 cutoff from 2.25 to 2.3625, so the outlier counts are buffered counts and must not be read as an exact BBP criticality test; defaults.yaml:147 max_tokens=20000 never binds at the study's num_samples=200 (~23272 tokens supplied) so wide models still cannot reach the 4*D tokens the g25 family needs.

DOCUMENTATION: the docstring at rmt_bulk.py:407-425 correctly warns that the CORRELATION family is structurally blind to per-dimension variance, and the permutation null at :239-286 is the statistic that is actually defensible for spike content. The MP-based *_cov spike numbers should not be read as spike content on heteroscedastic activations; the file says so, the emitted key names do not.
